issue.title: Bug: docker-sonic-mgmt fails to build on master

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

When attempting to build the sonic-mgmt docker container, we get an error trying to install the built sonic-dash-api .deb packages:

```
<IPV6>  Step 22/60 : RUN dpkg -i debs/sonic-device-data_*.deb debs/libdashapi_*.deb
<IPV6>   ---> Running in 8860a8e95173
<IPV6>  Selecting previously unselected package sonic-device-data.
<IPV6>  (Reading database ... 68372 files and directories currently installed.)
<IPV6>  Preparing to unpack .../sonic-device-data_1.0-1_all.deb ...
<IPV6>  Unpacking sonic-device-data (1.0-1) ...
<IPV6>  Selecting previously unselected package libdashapi.
<IPV6>  Preparing to unpack .../libdashapi_1.0.0_amd64.deb ...
<IPV6>  Unpacking libdashapi (1.0.0) ...
<IPV6>  Setting up sonic-device-data (1.0-1) ...
<IPV6>  ^[[91mdpkg: dependency problems prevent configuration of libdashapi:
<IPV6>   libdashapi depends on libpython3.9 (>= 3.9.1); however:
<IPV6>    Package libpython3.9 is not installed.
<IPV6>
<IPV6>  dpkg: error processing package libdashapi (--install):
<IPV6>   dependency problems - leaving unconfigured
<IPV6>  ^[[0m^[[91mErrors were encountered while processing:
<IPV6>   libdashapi
<IPV6>  ^[[0mThe command '/bin/sh -c dpkg -i debs/sonic-device-data_*.deb debs/libdashapi_*.deb' returned a non-zero code: 1
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Clone the sonic-buildimage repository and attempt to build the sonic-mgmt docker container.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Expected behavior: sonic-mgmt docker container builds successfully
Actual behavior: sonic-mgmt docker container fails to build with above error

resolution.title: Upgrade base of docker-sonic-mgmt to Ubuntu 24.04
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
The base image Ubuntu 20.04 of docker-sonic-mgmt is end of support now. Need to upgrade the base image and the dependent packages to address potential vulnerability issues.

DO NOT MERGE until https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/21045 is merged and cherry-picked to all current active branches.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
* Upgraded base image of docker-sonic-mgmt to Ubuntu 24.04.
* Upgraded the build environment to bookworm.
* Removed the logic of building flag `LEGACY_SONIC_MGMT_DOCKER`. All the sonic-mgmt branches are using python3 now. It's not necessary to build docker-sonic-mgmt to support python2. And python2 is end of support too.
* Version of python packages are not pinned down. This change has pros and cons.
  * Pros: Keep the docker-sonic-mgmt up to date to avoid future big version leap which could be difficult to handle.
  * Cons: Community package upgrade could have issue and cause regression.
* Version of ansible is pinned to 11.10.0. It's because pytest-ansible does not support the latest ansible due to https://github.com/ansible/pytest-ansible/issues/489
* Python packages are installed to /opt/venv by following the recommendation of Ubuntu 24.04.
* The dash-api package is reverted to install from source code. The dash-api debian package built in bookworm cannot be installed in Ubuntu 24.04 due to dependency issues.
* Default user "ubuntu" of Ubuntu 24.04 is removed from the image to avoid potential issues. For details, please refer to https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/20761. Skipped adding regular user. With this change, the image will only have root user. The `setup-container.sh` tool in the sonic-mgmt repository can add regular user. Recommend to use the `setup-container.sh` tool to create sonic-mgmt container.
* Improved the code for installing docker and azure-cli.
* Remove the build dependency of the `ptf` debian package. It's because the `ptf` package is installed by python pip.

#### How to verify it
After the upgrade, there are some compatibility issues. The compatibility issues are fixed in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/21045.
I am using that PR to verify that all PR test scripts can pass by using the upgraded docker-sonic-mgmt.

The fix in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/21045 is backward compatible. Backward compatibility is verified by PR testing of https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/20851
